source_caption:
Tom’s monologue to Cousin Greg is the ultimate sales pitch for the ultra-wealthy lifestyle, but the brilliant irony of Succession is that the show constantly proves him wrong. We watch these characters weaponize billions of dollars, wear pristine Armani armor, and operate completely above the law, yet not a single one of them ever looks genuinely happy, at peace, or content.

What makes Succession a 10/10 masterpiece is how it handles these moments. The show doesn't rely on flashy plot twists; it relies on sharp, biting dialogue and a brilliant, classical score to expose the moral rot inside the gilded cage. It’s a masterclass in writing that balances corporate satire with a deeply cynical study of power.
